reports.title: Disclaimer regarding forward-looking statements in the quarterly report

lines: The IEA now forecasts global oil demand to fall by 2.7 mb/d in 2026 and recover by 2.0 mb/d in 2027, leaving consumption 0.6% below 2025 levels.
For 2027, the IEA expects global oil supply to rise by 6.6 mb/d, well ahead of demand, as OPEC+ production recovers and non-OPEC+ output keeps growing.

desk.headline: Profit nearly doubles to $170.8m; Q4 74% booked at $55,148/day; plans to hand TORM stake to shareholders

other.label: Average fleet TCE
other.change: Q2 2026 rates were higher across all segments

results: Net profit rose to $170.8m ($0.34 a share) from $91.5m a year earlier, taking the nine-month total to $628.3m.
Vessel revenue rose 14% to $417.4m and TCE income to $277.5m, though average rates of $32,708/day were below Q2's war-driven peak.
About 259 off-hire days for scheduled drydockings weighed on earnings; the fee-based business made $6.3m.
Net asset value climbed $0.8bn to about $5.2bn ($9.80 a share) on higher ship values and the TORM stake.
A September share sale raised $289.1m net; net loan-to-value fell to 11.9% and cash reached $299.5m.

guidance.summary: Hafnia gives no profit guidance. It reports 74% of Q4 earning days already booked at an average $55,148/day, about 9,561 earning days in Q4, and plans to replace Q3 and Q4 cash dividends with a payout of its TORM shares.

items.new: TORM shares as special dividend (~$686.6m, ~$1.28/share at 17 Nov price); fallback cash payout of 90% of Q3 profit

points: Management sees product tanker fundamentals as strong into winter, helped by low diesel stocks and LR2s switching to crude trades, which shrinks the clean fleet.
It warned that a reopened Strait of Hormuz or Red Sea could unwind the shipping inefficiencies now propping up rates.
Hafnia dropped its pursuit of TORM; handing out the 19.8% stake depends on share-transfer arrangements with third parties, with a decision due by 25 Nov.
Eight purchase options worth about $235m will be exercised, below market value; ten MR newbuilds are due in 2028–29.
From 2027 dividends rise to 100% of profit when net loan-to-value is under 10%, though including newbuild commitments may lift the ratio.

Q4 spot rates on the uncovered 26% of days, and any change in Gulf and Red Sea shipping routes.
Use of cash for growth deals, purchase options and newbuild payments.
